items.title: A Day at the Farm
items.text: Last Saturday, our class visited a farm near the lake. First, we saw a group of sheep in a big field. The farmer told us that the sheep give wool, and he showed us the scissors he uses to cut it. Then we walked to the pond, where two geese were swimming with their babies. In the barn, some mice ran across the floor, and the children laughed. At lunch, we ate sandwiches with fresh tomatoes from the garden. Everyone agreed that the trip was fun, and many students wanted to visit again.

qs.q: What does the farmer use the scissors for?
o: To cut the grass near the pond
To cut the wool of the sheep
To cut the tomatoes for lunch
To cut the ropes in the barn
qs.why: 농부는 양털을 깎는 데 가위를 쓴다고 했어요.

qs.q: Where did the class see the geese?
qs.why: 거위는 연못(pond)에서 헤엄치고 있었어요.

qs.q: What does “their babies” mean in the passage?
qs.why: their는 geese를 가리키므로 babies는 새끼 거위예요.

qs.q: What can we guess from the last sentence?
o: The farmer was angry at the class
The trip was too short to learn
qs.why: 모두 즐거웠고 다시 가고 싶어 했으므로 여행을 즐겼다는 것을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Packing for Camp
items.text: Dear Mina, I am packing for our camping trip. My list is long! I need two pairs of socks, a warm jacket, and my glasses, because I cannot read the map without them. My mom says I should also bring a first-aid kit with some bandages. I will pack three flashlights, since the batteries in one of them are old. Do you have any good advice about food? I only have a little bread and some cheese at home. Maybe we can buy fruit on the way. I cannot wait to see the stars! Your friend, Jiho

qs.q: Why does Jiho write to Mina?
o: To share his list and ask about food
To say sorry for missing the trip
To invite her to his house for dinner
To ask her to bring a map
qs.why: 지호는 준비물을 알리고 음식에 대한 조언을 구하려고 편지를 썼어요.

qs.q: Why will Jiho pack three flashlights?
o: Mina asked him to bring three
His mom lost the other ones
The batteries in one are old
qs.why: 그중 하나의 건전지가 낡았기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does “them” refer to in “without them”?
qs.why: 지도를 읽는 데 필요한 것은 안경(glasses)이에요.

qs.q: Which food does Jiho have at home?
qs.why: 집에 빵과 치즈가 조금 있다고 했어요.

items.title: School Library Notice
items.text: Starting Monday, students may borrow up to three books at one time. Each book can be kept for two weeks. Please return your books on time, because other children are waiting for them. The library also has new computers and ten comfortable chairs near the window. Please do not bring food or drinks inside; crumbs and spills can hurt the books. If you lose a book, tell the librarian, and she will give you advice. Quiet readers are welcome all day, but no group meetings are allowed after school this month.

qs.q: How many books can a student borrow at one time?
qs.why: 한 번에 최대 세 권까지 빌릴 수 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why can students not bring food or drinks inside?
o: Crumbs and spills can hurt the books
The librarian is allergic to snacks
qs.why: 부스러기와 쏟은 음료가 책을 상하게 할 수 있다고 했어요.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the notice?
o: To invite students to a book party
To ask students to buy more books
To announce a change of teachers
To explain new rules and services
qs.why: 도서관의 새 규칙과 서비스를 알리는 공지예요.

qs.q: What is NOT allowed this month after school?
qs.why: 이번 달 방과 후에는 단체 모임이 허용되지 않아요.

items.title: Grandma's Kitchen
items.text: My grandmother lives in a small house with a big kitchen. Every weekend, my cousins and I go there. She keeps her knives on a high shelf, and we are not allowed to touch them. Instead, we wash the dishes and cut the bread. Her stories about the old days are my favorite part. She says that long ago, there were no supermarkets in her village, so people made their own cheese, and the whole family helped. Grandma's soup always has potatoes and onions, and it makes our weekends warm and happy.

qs.q: What is the writer's favorite part of the weekend visit?
o: Washing the dishes in the kitchen
Grandma's stories about the old days
qs.why: 글쓴이는 할머니의 옛날이야기가 가장 좋다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did people make their own cheese long ago?
o: There were no supermarkets in the village
Cheese was a gift from the farmers
qs.why: 그 마을에는 슈퍼마켓이 없었기 때문이에요.

qs.q: Why can the children not touch the knives?
o: Grandma wants to use them herself
The knives belong to a neighbor
They could be dangerous for children
qs.why: 칼은 위험할 수 있어서 아이들에게 만지지 못하게 한다고 추측할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the passage, “the whole family” means ___.
qs.why: whole은 '전체의'라는 뜻이라서 가족 모두를 뜻해요.

items.title: A Trip to the Zoo
items.text: At the zoo, we saw two giraffes, five monkeys, and a family of penguins. The zookeeper explained that the monkeys love bananas, but they also eat leaves and insects. The giraffes have very long necks, so they can reach leaves on tall trees. Penguins cannot fly, but they swim very fast. We took many photos, and Yuna drew pictures of the animals in her notebook. After the show, we bought small toys in the gift shop. On the bus home, everyone was tired but happy.

qs.q: Why can giraffes reach leaves on tall trees?
o: They are taller than the zookeeper
qs.why: 기린은 목이 아주 길어서 높은 나무의 잎에 닿을 수 있어요.

qs.q: What did Yuna do at the zoo?
o: She took photos of the penguins
She fed bananas to the monkeys
qs.why: 유나는 공책에 동물 그림을 그렸어요.

qs.q: Which sentence about penguins is true?
o: They fly higher than other birds
They live in the gift shop
They cannot fly but swim fast
qs.why: 펭귄은 날지 못하지만 빠르게 헤엄친다고 했어요.

qs.q: How did the students feel on the bus home?
qs.why: 버스에서 모두 피곤했지만 행복했다고 했어요.

items.title: An Email to Aunt Rosa
items.text: Hi Aunt Rosa, Thank you for having us next week! The weather news says it will rain on Tuesday and Wednesday, so we will bring raincoats and boots. My little sisters need dry shoes, so each of them is packing two extra pairs. I also have a small request: do you have any information about the town museum? We love old pictures and want to see them. If you have a map, please send us a photo of it. See you soon! Daniel

qs.q: Why will Daniel's family bring raincoats and boots?
o: Rain is expected on two days
The museum is near a river
qs.why: 화요일과 수요일에 비가 올 거라는 예보 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does Daniel ask Aunt Rosa for?
o: Some old pictures of the town
qs.why: 박물관에 대한 정보와 지도 사진을 부탁하고 있어요.

qs.q: How many extra pairs of shoes will each sister pack?
qs.why: 동생들은 각자 여분의 신발 두 켤레를 챙겨요.

qs.q: How does Daniel sound in the email?
qs.why: 감사 인사와 정중한 부탁이 있어 다정하고 예의 바르게 들려요.

items.title: The Lost Keys
items.text: Hana came home from school and could not find her keys. She looked in her bag, in her coat pockets, and under the sofa. Her brother Sam was playing games, and he did not look up. "Have you seen my keys?" she asked. "No," he said, "but you were in the kitchen this morning." Hana laughed. She went to the kitchen and found the keys next to her lunch box. She had put them down while she was washing the dishes. "I always lose things," she said. "Maybe I need a small box for my keys."

qs.q: Where did Hana find her keys?
qs.why: 열쇠는 부엌의 도시락 통 옆에 있었어요.

qs.q: Why did Hana put the keys down in the kitchen?
qs.why: 설거지를 하다가 열쇠를 내려놓았어요.

qs.q: What does Sam's answer show about him?
o: He was angry with his sister
He wanted to hide the keys
He did not know the kitchen
He was busy but still helped
qs.why: 게임 중이었지만 부엌에 있었다고 알려 주며 도와줬어요.

qs.q: What does Hana decide at the end?
o: To ask Sam to find her keys
To buy a new bag tomorrow
To keep her keys in a small box
qs.why: 열쇠를 넣을 작은 상자가 필요할지도 모른다고 했어요.

items.title: Sports Day
items.text: Our school Sports Day is next Friday. There are four teams: red, blue, green, and yellow. Each team has twenty students. The day begins with a race for the youngest children, and then the older students play soccer matches. Parents can sit on the benches near the field, but they must not enter the track. After lunch, there is a relay where the teams pass a baton, and the loudest cheers usually come from the green team. The winners will get medals, but every student will receive a bottle of water and a certificate. Please wear comfortable shoes and bring a hat.

qs.q: How many students take part in Sports Day?
qs.why: 네 팀에 각 팀 20명이므로 모두 80명이에요.

qs.q: What happens right after lunch?
qs.why: 점심 식사 후에 이어달리기가 있어요.

qs.q: What must parents NOT do?
qs.why: 부모님은 벤치에 앉을 수 있지만 트랙에 들어가서는 안 돼요.

qs.q: Who will get a certificate?
qs.why: 모든 학생이 물과 증서를 받는다고 했어요.

items.title: Why Do We Need Sleep?
items.text: Doctors say that teenagers need eight to ten hours of sleep every night. While we sleep, our bodies rest and our brains sort the information from the day. Students who sleep well often remember lessons better and feel happier. However, many teenagers stay up late because they use their phones or watch videos. Bright screens can make it harder to fall asleep. One simple piece of advice is to turn off all devices an hour before bed. Reading a book or listening to quiet music can also help. With good habits, most people will wake up with more energy.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How to choose a good mobile phone
Why sleep matters and how to sleep well
Which books are best before bed
qs.why: 수면이 왜 중요한지와 잘 자는 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Why do many teenagers sleep too little?
o: They use phones or watch videos late
They have too many early classes
Their doctors tell them to stay up
qs.why: 휴대폰이나 영상 때문에 늦게까지 깨어 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does “sort” mean in the passage?
qs.why: 뇌가 정보를 정리한다는 뜻이므로 sort는 '정리하다'예요.

qs.q: What advice does the writer give?
o: Eat a big meal at night
qs.why: 잠자리에 들기 한 시간 전에 기기를 끄라고 조언해요.

items.title: The Night Market
items.text: On Friday evenings, the street near my house becomes a night market. Sellers put up small tents and hang colorful lights above the stalls. You can buy hot snacks, such as fish cakes and sweet potatoes, and cold drinks from big boxes of ice. Some stalls sell handmade goods like scarves, socks, and phone cases. My aunt makes candles, and her customers are mostly tourists who want a souvenir. Although the market is crowded, people are friendly, and the sellers often give small gifts to children. I think the market shows the best side of our neighborhood.

qs.q: Who buys most of the candles that the writer's aunt makes?
qs.why: 고모의 손님은 대부분 기념품을 찾는 관광객이에요.

qs.q: What is the writer's opinion of the market?
o: It is too crowded to enjoy
It shows the best side of the town
qs.why: 글쓴이는 시장이 동네의 가장 좋은 모습을 보여 준다고 생각해요.

qs.q: Which item is sold at the handmade stalls?
qs.why: 수공예품 가게에서는 스카프, 양말, 휴대폰 케이스를 팔아요.

qs.q: What does “Although” show in “Although the market is crowded”?
qs.why: 붐비지만 사람들이 친절하다는 대조를 나타내요.

items.ex: I bought a pair of gloves yesterday.
items.exko: 나는 어제 장갑 한 켤레를 샀어요.

items.ex: We need new furniture for the living room.
items.exko: 우리는 거실에 놓을 새 가구가 필요해요.
